title: Official | Werder Bremen bring Moussa Ndiaye back to German football
description: Werder Bremen have officially completed the loan signing of Moussa Ndiaye from RSC Anderlecht, continuing an aggressive deadline-day overhaul of Daniel Thioune’s defensive flanks. The 24-year-old Se...
fullText:
Werder Bremen have officially completed the loan signing of Moussa Ndiaye from RSC Anderlecht, continuing an aggressive deadline-day overhaul of Daniel Thioune's defensive flanks. The 24-year-old Senegalese left-back joins for the entirety of the 2026/27 campaign. Werder have also secured an option to purchase Ndiaye permanently next summer.

His arrival gives Thioune another solution for two positions that, entering the season, were among the largest question marks in the squad. Ndiaye arrives primarily to compete with Olivier Deman at left-back, but can also serve in central defense.

Ndiaye spent the second half of last season on loan at Schalke 04 and made 14 appearances as the Royal Blues secured promotion back to the Bundesliga. That successful spell removes at least one element of uncertainty from the transfer. The Senegalese defender already knows the demands of German football and arrives with experience operating under pressure during a promotion race.

Ndiaye's background is nevertheless considerably broader. Before joining Anderlecht in 2022, the defender spent time in Barcelona's academy after moving into the Catalan club's U19 setup in 2020. He has subsequently developed into a flexible defensive option capable of covering both left-back and central defense.

"Moussa is a technically good and energetic full-back who has already gained experience in German football," Werder head of professional football Peter Niemeyer said. "He gives us another option on the left side of defense and can also be deployed as a center-back. We are convinced that he will noticeably strengthen our squad."

Head coach Daniel Thioune also emphasized the qualities that made Ndiaye attractive.

"Moussa fits our profile exactly: strong in the challenge, capable of contributing offensively and with a good balance between providing cover and pushing forward," Thioune said. "He has already shown that he can succeed in Germany and will give us greater variety on the left side."

title: Panthers GM Dan Morgan speaks on the surprising cut of one of his very first draft picks
description: Panthers GM Dan Morgan spoke about the "difficult" decision to part ways with 2024 third-round pick Trevin Wallace.
fullText:
In the spring of 2024, Dan Morgan made University of Kentucky linebacker Trevin Wallace the third draft pick of his tenure as Carolina Panthers general manager. And now, two years later, he's made him someone else's project.

Wallace, in perhaps the most surprising move of the team's cutdown from this past weekend, was not included on the initial 53-man roster for the 2026 campaign. The third-year defender would then hit waivers, and was claimed on Monday by the New York Jets.

Morgan, who spoke with reporters about the process on Tuesday, was asked about the decision to cut Wallace.

"Yeah, it's difficult," he stated. "Me and Trevin, we developed a really close relationship. He's been in my office multiple times, just watching tape together.

"I really wish him the best—obviously, getting claimed by the Jets. Really happy for him and his family, and a new start for him, a new direction. I know he's excited about it. But again, those decisions—they don't come easy."

Carolina selected Wallace in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He went on to make 20 starts over 25 games for the Panthers—amassing 125 combined tackles, 3.0 sacks, four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery.

This summer, the 23-year-old was pitted against fourth-year veteran Claudin Cherelus for the defense's second starting inside linebacker spot next to Pro Bowler Devin Lloyd. But neither won the job, as Morgan and Carolina have added free agents Bobby Okereke and Tyrel Dodson.

title: Chris Braswell's release shows how much the Bucs pass rush has changed
description: Chris Braswell's release shows how much the Bucs pass rush has changed
fullText:
Tampa Bay waived Braswell as part of its final cuts, ending his time with the team after just two seasons. Braswell appeared in all 34 games during that stretch but never developed into the pass rusher the Bucs hoped they were getting out of Alabama. He finished his time in Tampa Bay with 48 tackles, 2.5 sacks and five tackles for loss.

Moving on from a second-round pick still on their rookie deal is rare, but Braswell's release also says something about how different this position looks compared to a year ago. The Bucs kept five outside linebackers on their initial 53: Yaya Diaby, Rueben Bain Jr., Al-Quadin Muhammad, Anthony Nelson and David Walker. Diaby led Tampa Bay with seven sacks last season and finished ninth in the NFL in pressures. Bain was the 15th overall pick in April and gives the Bucs the blue-chip pedigree defender they've been missing. Muhammad arrives after recording 11 sacks with Detroit, while Walker has looked like one of Tampa Bay's most disruptive pass rushers throughout training camp after missing his rookie season with a torn ACL. Then there's Nelson, who has consistently provided value as a rotational defender and special teamer for the last few years and added 2.5 sacks during the preseason.

That left Braswell needing to give Tampa Bay a reason to keep a sixth outside linebacker, and it never really happened. His lack of development became even more noticeable as Walker emerged and the Bucs added legitimate talent around him. That's a big change from last season, when Tampa Bay finished with only 37 sacks and blitzed on 35 percent of its pass rush snaps, the third-highest rate in the NFL. The Bucs spent the offseason trying to build a front capable of creating pressure without Todd Bowles constantly sending the house. Now they'll enter the season with a deeper rotation than they've had in years and a much different-looking pass rush than the one they finished last season with.

title: Atletico Madrid hijacking Juventus move for Nicolás Tagliafico
description: Juventus’ delay in completing a move for Nicolás Tagliafico could cost them, as Atletico Madrid are closing in on hijacking their move for the Lyon star.Juve have an agreement in place with the def...
fullText:
Juventus' delay in completing a move for Nicolás Tagliafico could cost them, as Atletico Madrid are closing in on hijacking their move for the Lyon star.

Juve have an agreement in place with the defender on personal terms, and he is keen to join them before the transfer window closes today. However, Juventus only made their move for Tagliafico because Atalanta want to sign Juan Cabal, who is viewed as the replacement for the Colombian.

So far, La Dea have not completed their move for the Bianconeri star, meaning Juventus have also been unable to finalise their move for Tagliafico. The delay could now see them miss out on signing the Argentine defender.

According to Fabrizio Romano, Atletico Madrid have made contact to add Tagliafico to their squad and are advancing in talks to make the move happen.

The Spanish club only firmed up their interest in the defender today, but they could now secure his signature because Juventus are still waiting for Atalanta to complete their move for Cabal.

That development has left the Bianconeri in a difficult position. They have already agreed personal terms with Tagliafico, and the defender wants to move to Turin, but Juventus cannot complete the transfer until they have resolved Cabal's situation.

(Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images)

It is a frustrating situation for the Bianconeri, who need to act quickly if they want to prevent Atletico from taking advantage of their delay. The Spanish club have entered the race at a crucial moment and could now benefit from Juventus' inability to complete the necessary steps.

Juventus have wanted to offload Cabal for a long time, and his departure remains important because they need to create space for Tagliafico in their squad. Atalanta's interest appeared to provide the solution, but the move has not yet been completed.

With the transfer window closing today, there is very little time for Juventus to resolve the situation. They must now hope Atalanta completes their move for Cabal quickly, allowing the Bianconeri to proceed with Tagliafico before Atletico Madrid can secure the Argentine.

Tagliafico remains keen on joining Juventus, but the club's delay has opened the door for Atletico Madrid to make their move.

title: ‘They Dream With Me’ — Gabriela Fujimoto Details Unbreakable Family Bond Before Return At ONE Fight Night 47
description: The Brazilian atomweight phenom returns to action against Macarena Aragon this Friday.
fullText:
For Gabriela "Gabi" Fujimoto, martial arts has never been a solitary pursuit. Every step of her career carries her family's fingerprints, providing a shield that has anchored her since childhood.

That support system now travels with her into her next crucial test. The 23-year-old Brazilian phenom returns to the ring against Macarena Aragon, looking to bounce back in a women's atomweight MMA clash at ONE Fight Night 47 on Prime Video.

The highly anticipated event broadcasts live in U.S. primetime from the historic Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, this Friday, September 4.

Born in Mogi das Cruzes, Fujimoto proudly calls her parents Sansei, honoring their heritage as third-generation Japanese descendants in Brazil. Her father introduced her to karate at just four years old, setting her on a lifelong path that eventually prompted the regional champion to relocate to Rio de Janeiro to refine her craft.

While MMA is often considered an individual battle fought alone in the gym and inside the ring, Fujimoto has never known it that way. Her family's presence remains woven into every high and low of her journey.

The São Paulo native explained:

"My relationship with my family is incredible and very unique. They have supported me from the very beginning, and they have built this journey with me.

"My father, my mother, my brother, and I have always shared the same dream, and I'm very proud to honor that."

Competing against elite opposition already carries pressure, and doing so under family expectation could easily compound that weight.

As her skills evolve on the global stage, however, Fujimoto's mental approach remains steady. That composure stems directly from the support surrounding her.

"They have never pressured me or demanded that I win. What they have always asked of me is to give my best in everything I choose to do, and they have always made sure I know that they will be by my side no matter what happens."

That foundation faced a stern examination in her promotional debut. Her perfect 7-0 record was shattered on her birthday when divisional mainstay Jihin "Shadow Cat" Radzuan stopped her via third-round TKO at ONE Fight Night 40 this past February.

The sting of that first professional loss ran deep, but her family's voice in her corner softened the blow.

The Team KO Squad affiliate reflected:

"That is one of the things that gives me the strength to keep going. I fight for myself because this is my dream, but especially for them, because they dream with me.

"Everything I've achieved is also a reflection of everything we've built together."

Intrigue currently surrounds ONE Championship's women's divisions. At the top of Friday's marquee event, former three-sport ruler Stamp Fairtex battles Selina "Teep Queen" Flores under Muay Thai rules, while the atomweight mixed martial arts throne sits vacant after former titleholder Denice "The Menace" Zamboanga relinquished her crown.

Gabriela Fujimoto knows she still has work ahead after a rocky start to her ONE tenure. Still, her ultimate ambition of competing for 26 pounds of gold has never wavered, and the Brazilian standout savors every step along the way.

"It's very exciting to know that the atomweight division has an opportunity for a new champion. Of course, becoming a World Champion is one of my biggest goals, and I want to be part of that picture."

That ambition begins with a bid for redemption against Macarena Aragon. While the future holds promise, Fujimoto keeps her blinders firmly on for now.

Her sole mission heading into September 4 is proving she belongs on the global stage.

"But right now, my focus is completely on Macarena. I'm not looking past her. I want to go in there, perform at my best, and show the evolution I've made since my last fight.

"If I can make a statement and put myself closer to that title opportunity, even better. But first, I have a fight to win."

title: What We Learned About College Football in Week 0
description: North Carolina is better – but probably not very good Hats off to Bill Belichick and the Tar Heels for topping TCU 15-10 in week 0, after being completely dismantled by the Horned Frogs to kick off the 2025 season. The defense has shown signs of improvement, especially along the defensive line. However, TCU’s offense […]
fullText:
North Carolina is better – but probably not very good

Hats off to Bill Belichick and the Tar Heels for topping TCU 15-10 in week 0, after being completely dismantled by the Horned Frogs to kick off the 2025 season. The defense has shown signs of improvement, especially along the defensive line. However, TCU's offense seems to be a bit of a mess, and were held scoreless after scoring 10 points in their first two possessions. UNC also has some work cut out for them on offense and needs to find ways to generate more explosive plays. It was a nice start, but not sure UNC will go very far in year two of the Belichick experiment.

USC and Florida State had similar outcomes, but very different games

USC took down San Jose State, 42-26, while Florida State earned a week one victory over New Mexico State, 34-17. Neither outcome looks all that impressive, but the final scores are a bit deceiving. The Trojans built an early lead, then took their foot off the gas in the second half. The starters were out of the game by the fourth quarter, helping San Jose State come away with a 23-7 output in the final stanza. Meanwhile, Florida State could not pull away from New Mexico State and were forced to play four quarters. USC sure looked like they are a playoff contender, while Florida State may finish with yet another losing season – and be searching for a new head coach at some point this fall.

Virginia may be sticking around for a while

Virginia just missed out on the playoffs last season after losing to Duke in the ACC Championship Game. It was a nice story, but many dismissed the Cavaliers as a one-year wonder. In fact, they only appeared on one ballot in the preseason AP poll. However, it sure looks like they will have a number next to their name soon, and could be in the thick of the race for the ACC crown again. The offense looked sharp and the defense completely dominated NC State in what was expected to be a competitive contest. In case you were wondering, Beau Pribula had an enticing stat line while leading the team in passing and rushing – 9 of 11 for for two touchdowns and no interceptions, with another 110 yards on the ground on 15 carries.

Memphis has an early lead on the playoff race

Both UNLV and Memphis had their sights set on the playoffs this year – and the Tigers got a huge boost with their 27-21 victory over the Rebels. This will set up a huge showdown on Sept. 12 when Memphis visits Boise State. Charles Huff has been working his way up the coaching ranks, and may be a P4 head coach in 2027.

title: Charlton loan Fullah to MK Dons after signing new deal
description: Charlton midfielder Ibrahim Fullah joins Mk Dons on loan after agreeing a new contract with his parent club.
fullText:
Midfielder Ibrahim Fullah has joined MK Dons on loan after signing a new three-year contract with parent club Charlton Athletic.

The 19-year-old will spend the rest of this season at Stadium: MK after making 14 senior appearances for Charlton in 2025-26.

He scored his first two goals for the London club in League Cup ties against Stevenage and Cambridge United but has not previously had a loan spell elsewhere.

"The key for Ibrahim now is to get exposure to regular first-team football and continue his development in a competitive environment," said Dons sporting director Liam Sweeting.

On his new contract, Fullah told the Charlton website: "It's another step in the right direction and I just can't wait to kick on."

Both clubs are in action on Wednesday evening, with Charlton away to West Brom in the Championship and MK Dons travelling to Wigan in League One.

title: Will Odell Beckham Jr. get No. 13 back from Giants teammate?
description: Beckham is currently wearing No. 3 for the Giants
fullText:
Odell Beckham Jr. is back on the New York Giants a decade after his last Pro Bowl appearance with the franchise. Much has changed since then, with Jaxson Dart now the quarterback, John Harbaugh the coach and Beckham wearing... No. 3.

Yes, Beckham isn't wearing the iconic No. 13 jersey he graced the cover of Madden 16 with. Fourth-year receiver Jalin Hyatt has worn No. 13 since 2023 after publicly securing Beckham's blessing at the time. It's made for quite an awkward situation.

ROCK OUT ONE THREE @jalinhyatt 🚀

The Giants cut their roster to 53 on Sunday, with general manager Joe Schoen opting to keep Beckham on the regular-season roster over Hyatt, who signed to the practice squad. Still, Hyatt isn't letting Beckham get No. 13 back just yet.

Beckham recently admitted to reporters the number situation remains on his mind with the season opener approaching on Sept. 13.

"I think we all know what (No. 13) means to me, and there definitely will be some conversations," Beckham said. "I'll just say we'll see, but it would be an honor and a privilege to put that back on."

Hyatt has not lived up to the lofty standards Beckham set in No. 13. The former Tennessee star has 36 catches for 470 yards and 0 touchdowns through three seasons, and he didn't start a single game for the receiver-depleted Giants in 2025. He's struggled to run routes at the NFL level after relying on his speed in college.

Beckham isn't expected to play a huge role for the 2026 Giants, but him even making the roster at age 33, after several major injuries, is a feel-good story for the Giants. We'll soon see whether his New York reunion comes with his preferred number.

title: Red Sox, Phillies among 4 teams who could trade for Angels' Zach Neto this winter
description: Neto was a popular trade chip for the Angels.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Angels held on to shortstop Zach Neto at the trade deadline.

Evidently, the AL West club did not feel that the offers for Neto met their asking price, per FanSided's Robert Murray.

Though Los Angeles' asking price was likely high. Neto is on pace for his third consecutive 20-20 season while playing well below-average defense at shortstop.

"What was said about [Reid] Detmers above applies for Neto: there was massive interest in Neto, the Angels listened, but no team met the very high asking price," Murray wrote Tuesday.

The Boston Red Sox were rumored to be one of the contending clubs with interest in Neto at the deadline. Murray added that the AL East organization could reengage with the Angels this offseason.

"The Angels are once again in position to listen on Neto again in the winter, and the teams that make sense include the Boston Red Sox, Philadelphia Phillies, Milwaukee Brewers, Tampa Bay Rays and many others," Murray wrote. "At 25 and not a free agent until 2030, he's already hit 81 homers and 238 RBI in four major-league seasons while establishing himself as a franchise shortstop. He'd arguably be the best player on the market."

MORE:Cubs trade deadline addition Clay Holmes likely to opt out of $12M 2027 player option

The Angels are going nowhere fast, preparing to miss the postseason for the 12th consecutive season.

Unless the front office plans to offer Neto a contract extension in the near future, trading him this winter may be what's best for the Angels.

As Murray mentioned, the Red Sox and Phillies could be two teams to keep an eye on in the Neto sweepstakes.

title: How Long Is Willson Contreras Out? Hamstring Injury Updates, Return Timeline for Red Sox First Baseman
description: Here are the latest updates on Willson Contreras' status and how long he could be out for following his latest injury.
fullText:
How Long Is Willson Contreras Out? Hamstring Injury Updates, Return Timeline for Red Sox First Baseman originally appeared on NESN. 

One of the Red Sox's most reliable hitters will miss some action to start September, as Willson Contreras was placed on the 10-day injured list on Monday, August 31.

The stint appeared inevitable for the slugger, who has endured bruises and a cold streak the last month of the season. Boston recalled Mickey Gasper from Triple-A Worcester to replace him.

Before the injury, Contreras was slashing .274/.384/.516 with a .900 OPS and 26 home runs. However, he was hitting .217 in August, going hitless in five of his last seven games. Contreras also ranks third in hit by pitches (HBP), so this upcoming IL stint wasn't much of a surprise.

How long exactly will Contreras be out for the Red Sox? Here are the latest updates on Contreras' status and how long he could be out following his latest injury.

Per a statement, Contreras was placed on the 10-day IL due to a left hamstring strain.

MassLive's Chris Cotillo reported in early August that the injury was bothering him for a while. He felt it when he got booed after he didn't run to first base in the middle of August, grabbing at his hamstring in the process.

Contreras has dealt with injuries throughout the season, missing a few games after getting hit in the foot.

"I don't want to paint the picture that it's like something way worse happened. Just a recurrence of the same thing," interim manager Chad Tracy said regarding Contreras via MLB.com. "The triple, [late in the second game of Saturday's] doubleheader, a hard run there. It creeps up again. And he played [Sunday], and just with some irritation again.

"It's just to the point where if we need to give him another few days to let it calm down, we're getting to a point where it's tough to be short bodies."

The injury may have come at an inconvenient time for a team looking to jump over the Rays in the AL East. However, Contreras may only need the ten days to recover before rejoining the Red Sox.

The Red Sox may continue to rest their top contributors as the season winds down. Tracy recently decided to skip Sonny Gray's turn in the rotation to give the AL Cy Young favorite some rest.

title: Pakistan cricket in chaos: Misbah-ul-Haq resigns as PCB selector amid Test squad shake-up
description: Misbah-ul-Haq has stepped down from his role in the Pakistan Cricket Board's selection committee amid a significant shake-up of the Test team and coaching positions. After facing backlash from recent losses to England, several players and coaches have been dismissed, paving the way for five uncapped players to join the Test squad. Misbah's exit further complicates the current challenges within Pakistan cricket.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq has offered his resignation from the Pakistan Cricket Board's (PCB) national selection committee, adding another dramatic twist to the turmoil surrounding the Test side after a sweeping overhaul of the squad and coaching staff.

According to Geo News, sources close to Misbah said the former cricketer had informed the PCB of his decision and would serve a notice period before formally stepping down. Cricinfo also reported that Misbah had offered his resignation, although the PCB is yet to accept it.

The development comes just a day after the PCB announced wholesale changes to the Pakistan Test squad and coaching staff following the team's heavy 194-run defeat to England at Lord's.

The timing of Misbah's decision has raised questions over the selection committee's role in the PCB's latest overhaul. According to the reports, Misbah was apparently not consulted despite being part of the national selection committee when the board decided to make major changes to the squad and coaching staff.

The PCB released seven players from the Test squad ahead of the third Test against England at Edgbaston, starting September 9. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamer Jamal, Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad were among those released.

Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also removed as head coach and bowling coach respectively.

The PCB subsequently brought in white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and bowling coach Ashley Noffke to work with the Test side for the remainder of the England tour.

Cricinfo further reported that Misbah has decided to step down from his role as a batting consultant at the National Cricket Academy in Lahore, where his contract required him to work for 180 days a year.

The extent of Pakistan's overhaul was further highlighted by the inclusion of five uncapped players in the squad for the third Test.

Arafat Minhas, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Saad Baig, Mohammad Imran Randhawa and Razaullah have been added, while Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have also been brought into the group. The latter two have a combined experience of only 10 Test matches.

The sweeping changes followed Pakistan's innings-and-103-run defeat in the first Test before England won the second by 194 runs. The back-to-back defeats left Pakistan 0-2 down in the three-match series and staring at a potential 3-0 clean sweep.

Misbah was appointed to the four-member national selection committee in March alongside Aaqib Javed, Sarfaraz Ahmed and Asad Shafiq.

The former captain has previously held several senior positions within the PCB. He was appointed head coach and chief selector in 2019, before stepping down as chief selector in October 2020 and eventually leaving the head coach's position in 2021.

He returned to the PCB setup as an adviser in 2023 under the then ad hoc management committee headed by Zaka Ashraf. He was later appointed one of five mentors for the men's Champions Cup and also worked with women's domestic teams.

Last month, Misbah coached the Pakistan Gold side to victory in the 50-over National Champions Cup in Multan under captain Shaheen Afridi.

His reported resignation comes at a particularly difficult time for Pakistan cricket. The Lord's defeat was their 15th loss in their last 20 Tests, while they currently sit at the bottom of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 standings.

Pakistan squad for Birmingham Test against England: Babar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ali, Muhammad Imran, Mohammad Imran Jnr, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wk), Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicketkeeper), Saim Ayub, Sajid Khan, Saud Shakeel, Shan Masood, Abdullah Shafique, Ubaid Shah.

title: Chicago Fire sign Georgian midfielder Anzor Mekvabishvili
description: TRACKER STATUS: SigningChicago Fire FC have acquired midfielder Anzor Mekvabishvili from Romanian top-flight side Universitatea Craiova, the club announced Tuesday.The 25-yea...
fullText:
TRANSFER TRACKER STATUS: Signing

Chicago Fire FC have acquired midfielder Anzor Mekvabishvili from Romanian top-flight side Universitatea Craiova, the club announced Tuesday.

The 25-year-old Georgian international is under contract through the 2028-29 MLS season with an option for 2029-30.

Mekvabishvili has tallied 15g/20a in 231 matches across Universitatea Craiova and Dinamo Tbilisi in his home country. He's won four club titles, including the Romanian double in 2025-26.

Internationally, Mekvabishvili has earned 33 caps with Georgia. He was a key starter during their Euros 2024 appearance.

"We're excited to add a player of Anzor's pedigree to the club," said Chicago director of football and head coach Gregg Berhalter. "He is a proven competitor whose experience at both the international level and in European competition will be a valuable asset to our group.

"Being recognized as Player of the Year on a championship-winning team speaks to the consistency, leadership and impact he brings. We believe he will play an important role in strengthening our midfield and raising the level of the squad."

Mekvabishvili is Chicago's second major signing this summer, following iconic Polish striker Robert Lewandowski.

The Fire are third in the Eastern Conference (37 points) and on track for a second-straight Audi MLS Cup Playoffs trip.

title: Maloney on Celtic working 'on key positions', left-back area, Sinisalo's challenge & Hatate future
description: Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney has been speaking to the media before Wednesday's Scottish Premiership meeting with Aberdeen.  Maloney says the Scottish champions are "really happy" with their four summer signings so far and "there's some key positions that we still need a bit of work on in the next couple of days".  The assistant manager says "the profiles of what we need in those positions are really important, that we do replace what we've lost", citing Arne Engels' recent departure.
fullText:
Celtic assistant manager Shaun Maloney has been speaking to the media before Wednesday's Scottish Premiership meeting with Aberdeen. Here are the key points.

Maloney says the Scottish champions are "really happy" with their four summer signings so far and "there's some key positions that we still need a bit of work on in the next couple of days".

The assistant manager says "the profiles of what we need in those positions are really important, that we do replace what we've lost", citing Arne Engels' recent departure. "The club's working really hard to give us those types of players," Maloney added.

"Some really key positions in the squad, you're looking at three or four and if there's anymore than that, that'll be really, the thinking of the club will be for the future," Maloney said.

When asked about the possibility of a loan capture of teenage Chelsea forward Shim Mheuka, the assistant says, "it's pretty difficult to talk about" prospective signings and "nothing's confirmed with anyone".

With goalkeeper Sam Johnstone linked with a season-long loan at Celtic, Maloney says the message to first-choice Viljami Sinisalo is: "You have to keep performing at the levels you are to keep the shirt."

Celtic "hope" to sign another left-back to compete with Kieran Tierney, says the assistant manager.

And Maloney revealed "it's possible" Japan midfielder Reo Hatate could move on from the club.

The assistant expects Wednesday's game "to be a really tough game" and urges Celtic "to be more aggressive", adding: "We want more without the ball."

Team news: striker Kasper Hogh and defender Tierney will "struggle" to be fit to face Aberdeen but could make the weekend while forward Callum Osmand faces "a few weeks" out with an ankle injury.

title: Marc Casado in talks to leave Barcelona for Deportivo

fullText:
Barcelona midfielder Marc Casado is reportedly in talks to join La Liga side Deportiva de A Coruna before the close of the transfer window later today.

Casado has been looking for an exit and could now be set to stay in the Spanish top flight, according to Diario Sport.

Deportivo are trying to bring in Casado on a season-long loan and the midfielder is now considering heading to Antonio Hidalgo's side.

The Galicians are back in La Liga this season and have made a good start, drawing against Elche and Malaga and beating Valencia.

title: Sunderland not giving up on Malick Fofana pursuit
description: Sunderland AFC are not giving up in the frantic race to sign Belgium international winger Malick Fofana (21), according to L’Equipe. The Black Cats thought they had a clean run at signing Fofana aft...
fullText:
Sunderland AFC are not giving up in the frantic race to sign Belgium international winger Malick Fofana (21), according to L'Equipe. The Black Cats thought they had a clean run at signing Fofana after agreeing a Deadline Day €35m for the in-demand left-winger. Sunderland had even booked a medical for Fofana. But earlier today, Crystal Palace looked to have hijacked their Premier League rivals' deal in outbidding their offer, with Lyon agreeing a €39m transfer package.

The outlet reported that a phone call from Palace manager Pierre Sage – who oversaw Fofana's development at Lyon – swayed the Belgian towards signing for the Selhurst Park. But there is another twist in the tale. L'Equipe now reports that Sunderland haven't given up their pursuit of the left-sided winger. The Black Cats have reportedly revived the deal by offering much higher commissions to the player's agents.

Furthermore, although Fofana is in London, he's yet to undergo a medical with Crystal Palace, and the Eagles are currently left in the dark regarding the player's whereabouts.

fullText:
Liverpool FC are reported to have made a last-ditch attempt in recent hours to sign Chelsea FC's Malo Gusto (23), according to information from RMC Sport.

However, their efforts proved fruitless, as the Reds were hoping to secure the Frenchman's signature on a loan deal without a mandatory buy-out clause, whilst their London counterparts were only willing to consider a permanent transfer.

These plans were quickly ruled out by Liverpool's management, who were unable to meet the financial demands set by the Blues for the 23-year-old.

Under contract with Chelsea until 2030, Gusto is therefore set to continue his spell there in the coming months, having established himself as a key member of the London club's squad – scoring three goals and providing 18 assists in 137 matches across all competitions.

Having started in the first three matches managed by Xabi Alonso this season, the French international – who has 16 caps – provided one assist.

title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Foster Edwards
description: Edwards made the big leagues when he was just 21. The rest of his career didn’t go well.
fullText:
If the name Foster Edwards doesn't immediately inspire awe in your mind, are you really a Yankees fan? Just kidding. Edwards, a right-handed pitcher, was a Yankee for all of two games in 1930, and he didn't really do anything to ensure that his name would be etched onto history during those appearances.

Yet he was a Yankee all the same, and as a writer for the Internet's most devoted (citation needed) Yankees fan site, I will try my darnedest to celebrate his birthday and career. After all, he was the only player in franchise history to be born on September 1st, and here we are at the outset of September! It's Foster's lucky day.

Foster Hamilton "Eddie" Edwards
Born: September 1, 1903 (Holstein, IA)
Died: January 4, 1980 (Barnstable, MA)
Yankees Tenure: 1930

Long before Ben Rice stepped onto a diamond and even prior to 1930s standout third baseman Red Rolfe, it was Edwards who became the first former Dartmouth standout to play for the Yankees. Following his graduation from Central High School in Hennepin, Minnesota, Edwards pitched at Dartmouth from 1924-25 and stayed in New England for the beginning of his pro career. Edwards recorded a 4.02 ERA in 112 innings across 21 games for the Worcester Panthers of the Eastern League, and 1925 also saw him make his MLB debut.

When Edwards toed the rubber for the Boston Braves on July 2, 1925, he was still just 21 years old. His task was to mop up a game where the Braves were already losing 15-2 to the Brooklyn Robins in the seventh inning. He managed to finish the game, but that was about where the positives ended. He gave up five runs (two earned) on six hits and a walk. That was his only appearance in the majors that year.

To his credit, Edwards put together a very strong campaign in 1926, albeit mainly for the Providence Rubes, who had succeeded Worcester in the Eastern League. He went 25-8 with a 2.95 ERA across 259 innings, leading the EL in wins. He would return to the major leagues in September, going 2-0 with a 0.72 in three starts and 25 innings pitched. It seemed like he was poised to take bigs by storm.

Alas, that did not happen. The following year, Edwards went 2-8 with a 4.99 ERA as the Braves relegated him to relief duty in the latter half of the season. His struggles continued in 1928, and after the season, he decided to retire and enter the grocery business. However, Edwards evidently wasn't quite ready to give up, and the Yankees must have seen something in him, as they picked him up prior to the 1930 season.

The 26-year-old impressed the club in spring training and was on the roster early that year, alongisde luminaries like Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig. Maybe in an alternate universe, Edwards might have rewarded the Yankees handsomely, playing a role on those fabled 1930s squads and carving out a name for himself in pinstriped lore.

That didn't come to pass in this one, though. Edwards gave up four runs in 1.2 innings of work across two early season relief appearances, and that was all the Yankees needed to see before effectively banishing him to the minors. And that was all she wrote.

Sometimes—heck, most times—the things you set your heart on don't work out. I'm sure Edwards had bigger aspirations for his career—why else would he have returned to pitch for the Yanks after spending an entire year out of pro ball? But it just didn't happen. He tried, though, and I think that's a legacy worth hanging your hat on — to have tried something with your whole heart. That counts, even if you don't get what you want in the end.

Happy birthday, Foster. Rest easy.

See more of the "Yankees Birthday of the Day" series here.

title: “A massive win” Arteta delighted Arsenal won at tough Villa Park
description: Mikel Arteta believes Arsenal’s win at Villa Park yesterday was a massive result for the team, as the Gunners demonstrated why they are the defending champions.Villa Park is one of the hardest place...
fullText:
Mikel Arteta believes Arsenal's win at Villa Park yesterday was a massive result for the team, as the Gunners demonstrated why they are the defending champions.

Villa Park is one of the hardest places for any team to visit because Aston Villa have a strong team and a very good manager who knows what it takes to secure results.

The Villans have lost several of their best players during this transfer window, yet they still managed to field a team capable of causing Arsenal problems. They did everything possible to prevent the Gunners from finding much joy in the match, forcing Arteta's side to work extremely hard before eventually finding a way to win.

It was not a classic performance from either team, but Arsenal will be delighted to have secured the result as they look ahead to more victories. The Gunners showed determination and resilience to claim all three points from a difficult fixture.

Arteta was delighted and relieved that his players returned from the encounter with all three points. The Spaniard also highlighted the contribution of Arsenal's substitutes, who helped the team see out the victory.

"Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. I think we deserved it. A great squad performance, because when 11 wasn't enough the finishers game in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

(Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Arteta also remembered Arsenal's previous defeat at Villa Park, making this victory even more satisfying for the Gunners. The painful manner of that loss had clearly remained with the manager and his players.

"Last year we lost here in a really difficult way, with the last kick of the game. And that was still in the tummy."

The victory therefore carried significance beyond the three points. Arsenal had struggled at Villa Park previously, but they showed the character required to overcome another difficult challenge.

Villa made the match uncomfortable and restricted Arsenal's attacking opportunities, yet the Gunners remained patient and continued working until they found the decisive breakthrough.

For Arteta, the result demonstrated the strength of his squad and the importance of having players capable of making an impact from the bench. Arsenal can now take confidence from the victory as they continue their title defence.

title: Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming
description: The Golden State Warriors have rounded out their roster for the upcoming season. Former Warriors NBA champion, Steph Curry's former teammate just gave a little insight into when he thinks the four-time champion will retire.
fullText:
Ex-Warriors NBA champion gives Steph Curry retirement prediction with regular season looming originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Golden State Warriors know that Steph Curry is nearing the end of his career one way or another. The four-time NBA champion will go down as one of the greatest players to ever play the game.

Golden State and Curry have an important decision to make, as the superstar is eligible for a contract extension.

"What the terms of a new extension look like for Curry will be completely up to him, as the Warriors are prepared to offer their star whatever he wants. If Steph wants the full $136.7 million through the 2028-29 season, he will get that. If he wants to take a discount to help the team, GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. will have no problem with said deal," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

When Curry agrees to the extension will also be important. If he waits, it could potentially benefit the Warriors financially and give the organization more flexibility moving forward.

"There's still players becoming contract extension eligible. By next week you'll start to see Steph Curry's name come up. On the 29th of August he's extension eligible for his contract. I have argued that it should be considered that Steph doesn't sign the extension yet. If he chooses to sign right now, he could get two years at $140 million. Obviously if that's what he says he wants, you give it to him. But if he doesn't sign his contract extension right now the Warriors could have over $100 million in salary cap space next summer," ESPN's Brian Windhorst said.

Curry, like many of the NBA's greatest players, is getting closer to retirement. Former Golden State teammate and champion Matt Barnes recently revealed how long he believes it could be until Curry calls it a career.

"I think Steph is going to ride the ship until it sinks, similar to what Kobe did," Barnes said.

The hope is that the Warriors can make one final championship run before Curry eventually retires. LeBron James is still playing at 41 years old, so Curry could very well want to extend his career for as long as possible as well.

The former MVP remains one of the best shooters in the league, and outside of some injuries, he still looks capable of performing at an elite level. With that in mind, Curry could potentially have another two or three seasons before age begins to significantly catch up with him.

title: Colts GM Chris Ballard on Keenan Allen: Give him some grace
description: Wide receiver Keenan Allen remains a member of the Colts after being arrested for operating a vehicle while intoxicated over the weekend and it doesn't appear that's going to change in the coming days.
fullText:
Wide receiver Keenan Allen remains a member of the Colts after being arrested for operating a vehicle while intoxicated over the weekend and it doesn't appear that's going to change in the coming days.

General Manager Chris Ballard said at a Tuesday press conference that Allen will be in the team's lineup for their Week 1 game against the Ravens. He also said Allen's history in the NFL shows no sign of this being an issue that changes how the team feels about him.

"I'm not going to comment on what happened," Ballard said. "What I'm gonna tell you is good people make mistakes. He's a tremendous human being, give him some grace and he'll work through the process of the legal system."

Ballard said that any discipline from the team will be handled in-house. Allen will also be subject to league discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy.

title: Josh Allen is highest-ranked QB in NFL’s Top 100 Players list
description: Allen has been named the No. 1 QB on this player-voted list
fullText:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has officially been ranked as the highest quarterback, according to the annual NFL Top 100 list.

Last week, Allen was among the five players left to be ranked after the league hit Number 95. The others: Matthew Stafford, the only other quarterback left on the list, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Miles Garrett, and Bijan Robinson.

The five remaining players in this year's NFL Top 100:

🔵 Josh Allen
🟡 Myles Garrett
🔴 Bijan Robinson
🟢 Jaxon Smith-Njigba
🟡 Matthew Stafford

Agree or disagree that these are the five best players in the league? pic.twitter.com/MyOMsSxMH9

On Monday, wide receiver Smith-Njigba got the nod. This morning it was Matthew Stafford listed at number four:

No. 4 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026…@RamsNFL QB Matthew Stafford! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/5MUoVrcCcS

That leaves Allen as the only quarterback left on the list.

Allen finished the 2025 season with 3668 yards and 25 touchdowns. His 102.2 passer rating was fifth best in the NFL – behind Lamar Jackson (103.8), Jared Goff (105.5), Matthew Stafford (109.2), and Drake Maye (113.5).

While many thought Maye should get the NFL's MVP honor, that went to Stafford. Now, Allen has beaten them both out for the NFL's final 2025 honor. Instead of talking heads making the decisions, players are. And we can assume, this means that NFL players fear Allen much more than Maye who finished at 11.

Remember, before the 2024 season, an ESPN article that surveyed 100-plus players listed Allen as the most overrated quarterback. He proceeded to win the NFL MVP that season. Last year, Allen was listed at No. 3 on this very list.

While we await his final placement, Bills fans can laud, taunt, relish, or however you choose to celebrate (aka rubbing it in to those rivals to our east), the fact that the best quarterback in the league plays in Buffalo.

title: What Colts GM Chris Ballard said on Keenan Allen arrest
description: Colts WR Keenan Allen was arrested for DUI hours after his preseason debut; here's what GM Chris Ballard said about the incident
fullText:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The Colts believe that veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen is a good person who made a mistake that led to his arrest over the weekend. Allen was charged with misdemeanors for operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated (OVWI) and OVWI endangering a person.

Allen, 34, will play in the team's season opener against Baltimore on Sept. 13, and he was participating in practice when the team returned to work Tuesday.

"I'm not going to comment on what happened, but what I'm going to tell you is good people make mistakes," Colts general manager Chris Ballard said. "He's a tremendous human being. Give him some grace, and he'll work through the process of the legal system."

The Colts do have ride-share services available to players to avoid Allen's situation.

Indianapolis has imposed its own consequences.

"We handled everything internally with us," Ballard said. "The rest is a league matter."

Allen has handled his reaction to the team well, according to Ballard.

"Like you'd expect a person who cares about other people to react," Ballard said.

The Colts did not consider releasing Allen, who signed late in training camp. Ballard said that the Colts handle every situation on a case-by-case basis, and although Allen is new to Indianapolis, the veteran receiver is a known commodity to the decision-makers inside the building.

"Fourteen years in the league with no issues," Ballard said. "Decorated career, decorated teammate. You know our relationship with Philip Rivers, Philip knows him, and Shane Steichen obviously has a relationship with him. ... We feel good, unequivocally about who Keenan is."

Asked repeatedly about Allen's mistake, Ballard emphasized the need to give Allen grace.

"That's one of our problems now (as a society), we don't give anybody grace," Ballard said. "Over time, he'll prove himself to the city."

Allen was arrested early Sunday morning around 1 a.m., just hours after he'd made his on-field debut for the Colts blocks away at Lucas Oil Stadium in the preseason finale. According to a public police report viewed by IndyStar, IMPD officers conducted a traffic investigation in the 100 block of S. Meridian Street after observing a vehicle sitting in a no-parking zone at 110 S. Meridian St. The officers then proceeded to speak with the driver, who they later identified as Allen "and noticed signs of intoxication," according to a statement from IMPD.

Following a further investigation, Allen was arrested on a pair of preliminary misdemeanor charges of operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated (OVWI) -- with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 or higher -- and OVWI endangering a person.

Allen spent more than 12 hours in police custody before he was released from the Marion County Arrestee Processing Center at 3:49 p.m. Sunday afternoon, according to inmate records. The Colts receiver now has an upcoming court date Sept. 16, three days after the Colts' season-opener at Lucas Oil Stadium against the Ravens.

title: Tua Tagovailoa caught in Instagram faux pas
description: It has been a rough time for Tua Tagovailoa in recent years and he needs all the public support he can get, even if it comes from himself. The Miami Dolphins cut Tua following the 2025 season after seeing a precipitous drop in form and struggles with injuries. In doing so, they ate an NFL-record…
fullText:
It has been a rough time for Tua Tagovailoa in recent years and he needs all the public support he can get, even if it comes from himself.

The Miami Dolphins cut Tua following the 2025 season after seeing a precipitous drop in form and struggles with injuries. In doing so, they ate an NFL-record $99.2 million in dead cap space to move on and start over.

Tagovailoa was able to find a new home with the Atlanta Falcons where he is competing with former first round draft pick Michael Penix Jr. for the starting job. While the Falcons haven't won the NFC South since 2016, some decent quarterback play to go along with their exciting skill position players could provide some serious competition in an open division.

However, that quarterback play has remained a huge question mark. And after neither quarterback won the job during the preseason, the Falcons have yet to name a starter with the regular season just a week away.

However, Tua Tagovailoa is at least still trying to win Falcons fans over, although his recent post on Instagram was the equivalent of a social media pick six.

Tagovailoa posted a picture of himself in a Falcons uniform with the caption "For the A." That is obviously not a story. However, the first comment underneath the post was himself commenting "We're so proud of you! You got this!" with a heart emoji. The comment was screenshotted and shared several times before it was finally deleted.

Tua forgot to switch to his burner pic.twitter.com/SrznFjLYJA

— Austin Latham (@AustinLatham25) September 1, 2026

It's easy to see this, point and laugh, and assume some kind of wider Kevin Durant burner activity that is ongoing where Tua Tagovailoa is scrolling the internet trying to silence critics and hype up his chances of winning the Falcons starting quarterback job. Of course, a much more logical explanation is that whoever is managing his social media accounts forgot to log back into his or her personal account before leaving the supporting message.

Still though, as innocuous as the truth probably is, it still stands as a symbol of Tua's fall down the NFL pecking order at quarterback. And the fact that he needs all the help and hope he can get in getting his career back on track.

The post Tua Tagovailoa caught in Instagram faux pas appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: Kevin Durant Says Some Of His Closest Friends Are 9-To-5 Workers He Met Through Video Games
description: Kevin Durant has been friends with his gaming group for almost a decade.
fullText:
Houston Rockets superstar Kevin Durant has been an avid gamer for years, and it turns out that hobby has led to him making some pretty special friends. During an episode of Boardroom Talks, Speedy Morman asked Durant whether he has made friends over video games and whether they know that it's actually him they're playing with.

"Yes, they hung out with me in my house," Durant said. "They'd been friends with me for damn near 10 years now… One of my best friends I met on the game… And it's like I trust this dude with anything. Like seriously. We hung out plenty of times. So, I'm like, 'Let me see what this dude really about.'"

With Durant regularly speaking to this person and his group of gamers during these sessions, he decided he had to meet them in person. When he did, he realized they were great people, and they are his friends to this day. While Durant is, of course, this big superstar, some of his friends have just regular day jobs.

"We got 9-to-5s," Durant said. "… And I'm like, 'How y'all got so much time to play the game with me?' My job is from 9 to 11 in the summer. I go to work, and I don't have to do that. I just go do that 'cause I love to do it. And I'm like, 'How y'all got so much time to play the game?' I'm just like, man, this my safe haven for real. This is what I do to decompress.

"It's 10 of us in a party," Durant continued. "We competitively playing the game. We communicating, trying to win. It's like when you think about it, it's good for the soul when you know after a long day at work when you come home with your homies and just vibe without having to go out and have a drink or make a big production out of it.

"So I definitely made some friends," Durant added. "Then I got 14-year-old little homies that I've been kicking it with. They'll come to a EYBL game, and I meet them there. It's a real community on there."

Durant said he has consistently played with about 50 people over the last six years. Many of them didn't realize at first that they were playing with him, but eventually put the pieces together. You can only imagine how shocked they'd be upon finding out.

With Durant's love for gaming, it's hardly surprising that he complains about his NBA 2K ratings almost every year. Most recently, the 37-year-old was mad about his mid-range shooting rating in NBA 2K27.

Durant has a 93 overall rating in the game, and you'd think he wouldn't be too pleased about that either. The 16-time All-Star averaged 26.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.9 blocks per game for the Rockets in 2025-26. He made the All-NBA Second Team and is still a force on the court despite his age.

While Durant continues to shine on the court, the end of his career isn't too far away. He hasn't planned everything he's going to do post-retirement, but did share one of his main goals. Durant wants to become the managing director of the USA Basketball Men's National Team. He's likely going to be involved in the game one way or the other.

title: Is Mike McCarthy overhauling the Steelers' cultural identity?
description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers lineman Willie Colon breaks down how head coach Mike McCarthy is reshaping the team's offense and culture.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are undergoing a distinct identity shift under new head coach Mike McCarthy, and former offensive lineman Willie Colon believes fans are witnessing a complete cultural overhaul.

Speaking on NFL Network's "Good Morning Football," Colon reflected on his time playing under legendary coaches Bill Cowher and Mike Tomlin before breaking down how McCarthy's approach marks a noticeable break from tradition.

"I was fortunate enough to go through a Bill Cowher training camp, where it was hard-nosed, volatile, and in your face," Colon shared. "Then a young, fresh-faced Mike Tomlin comes in, he turns boys into men in a week in training camp. This training camp was different for the Steelers. It was more about reps and volume and high tempo, and this was more about creating an ecosystem for these young quarterbacks."

"This training camp was different for the @steelers" 

- @willcolon66 on his former team now being led by Mike McCarthy 👀 pic.twitter.com/HeTtxezQCx

That tactical shift is reflected in roster construction. Pittsburgh opted to carry four quarterbacks while keeping just nine offensive linemen, a stark departure for a franchise historically rooted in ground-and-pound football and physical line play.

Colon raised eyebrows at that structural gamble, noting, "You want to kind of keep as many big, ugly guys up front to protect the old GOAT."

The roster dynamics reflect an offensive ambition focused on explosive passing play rather than traditional clock management. After ranking 15th in scoring, Pittsburgh is aiming for a top-tier offense. Defensive depth has also been reallocated, with the team keeping only three safeties on the initial roster.

While these unconventional moves create pre-season anxiety, Colon emphasized that organizational backing remains firm.

"This thing is happening right before our eyes, and for a lot of Steelers fans, they're trying to figure out if this is good, if it's not," Colon concluded. "Nobody knows until the ball rolls out there. But you have to trust Mike McCarthy. The Rooney's and the powers that be trust Mike McCarthy. So this whole culture, this whole branding, everything is revamping right before our eyes."

title: Warriors Fans Get Massive Steph Curry Update on Contract Talks and Retirement Plans
description: Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry closed last season on a sour note, falling to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament after Golden State stumbled to a 37-45 finish, its fewest wins since 2019-20. Now entering his 18th NBA season, the four-time champion is opening up about his future in the Bay Area, and [...]
fullText:
Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry closed last season on a sour note, falling to the Phoenix Suns in the play-in tournament after Golden State stumbled to a 37-45 finish, its fewest wins since 2019-20. Now entering his 18th NBA season, the four-time champion is opening up about his future in the Bay Area, and his latest comments carry far more weight than they first appear.

Speaking with NBC Sports Bay Area at the Workday Charity Classic in Palo Alto, Curry made his intentions clear just two days after becoming eligible for a new contract extension.

The 38-year-old guard is entering the final season of his current Golden State Warriors deal, worth 62.6 million dollars, and he is now able to sign a two-year extension worth roughly 136.7 million dollars.

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen," Curry said. "The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

The remark leaves little doubt about where Curry sees himself long term, even though the paperwork remains unsigned. General manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. has said Golden State wants a deal finalized before the season begins, but Curry appears content to let the process play out on its own schedule rather than rushing toward a deadline.

Curry's remarks arrive as Golden State tries to move past a rough 2025-26 season that ended with a play-in loss to the Suns. Analysts have questioned whether the current roster can get Curry back to the postseason, though he seems focused on continuity rather than promises.

He is entering his 18th NBA season alongside familiar faces like Draymond Green and Al Horford, with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody working back from knee injuries.

His wife Ayesha shares that same confidence about what comes next for the family. "I think we're going to be in for some fun surprises over the next couple of years," Ayesha Curry added.

Golden State opens training camp at BYU-Hawaii this fall, setting up a preseason slate that will offer the first look at how the roster fits together.

Golden State's preseason schedule opens October 4 against the Los Angeles Clippers, giving fans their first look at this new-look roster. With Curry firmly committed and an extension still pending, the Warriors head into camp focused on health, continuity and getting back into playoff contention this season.

title: Warriors to meet Clippers for preseason game in Hawaii

The Los Angeles Clippers and Golden State Warriors will have training camp in Oʻahu, Hawaii and play a preseason game at the University of Hawaii on Oct. 4.

title: Packers expect Josh Jacobs to play this season, prepared if he doesn’t
description: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst and coach Matt LaFleur discussed the legal situation surrounding running back Josh Jacobs.
fullText:
GREEN BAY – Before Brian Gutekunst decides Josh Jacobs' future with the Green Bay Packers, the general manager is intent on letting the legal process unfold.

Gutekunst said he's uncertain if Jacobs will play for the Packers this season after he was placed on the exempt list over the weekend, though he remains hopeful the running back will return to the field.

"Certainly we would expect that," Gutekunst said. "But we're going to let this process play out, and we'll be prepared either way."

Jacobs' immediate future is dependent on NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who holds sole authority in determining the indefinite timeline of a players' stint on the exempt list. If the Packers have any hints at how long that will be, they aren't sharing.

Gutekunst could inject more clarity if he were to release Jacobs, but he's in no rush to do so.

"I think we'll let the process play out before we make any kind of those decisions," Gutekunst said, when asked if Jacobs might be released, "but we'll see."

Jacobs was placed on the exempt list Aug. 30, two days after the Brown County Distract Attorney's office levied two misdemeanor charges resulting from a late May arrest. Jacobs' charges included one count of battery and another of criminal damage to property.

The District Attorney's report referenced video surveillance from Jacobs' home showing him throwing a woman to the ground, which resulted in a bump on the women's head. It also stated Jacobs destroyed the woman's phone.

Gutekunst said he has not seen the video evidence.

"Those are legal things going on right now," Gutekunst said. "So we'll let those play out. That's really not for us. At the appropriate times, if those things become available, we'll figure that stuff out when the time comes."

The exempt list allows for players to be in team facilities for meetings. Coach Matt LaFleur said Jacobs still will be around the team, and the team has not changed how it feels about its running back.

"I don't want to get too far into it," LaFleur said, "but I think we all have seen this guy. I have a lot of love and care for how is as a person, who he is as a teammate. Obviously a very unfortunate situation, but one that we have to deal with."

LaFleur said he doesn't know all the details of what happened, but he has had "many conversations" with Jacobs. The coach said he "believes" in Jacobs and "trusts him."

"I'm going to do that until proven otherwise," LaFleur said.

In the three months since Jacobs' arrest, Gutekunst said, he's closely monitored the Packers running back position, ready to augment the depth chart if necessary. On the same day Jacobs was placed on the exempt list, Gutekunst traded for Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson.

A third-round draft pick in 2025, Johnson rushed for 1,537 yards and 21 touchdowns as a college junior at Iowa. He quickly found himself buried behind veterans on the Steelers depth chart. Gutekunst is hopeful a change of scenery can benefit both sides.

"From the very beginning when this all kind of first transpired," Gutekunst said, "we've been looking at different options and investigating some things. Whether that's this summer, whether that's as training camp started, a lot of conversations. We knew kind of going into it that this might be a possibility. Once we got the information that we did, we kind of knew what the options were at the moment and made the decisions that we made.

"We're excited to get Kaleb in here. Obviously a young player with huge upside, and we're excited to get him into our environment and see what he can do."

Gutekunst acknowledged it will take time for Johnson to acclimate to coach Matt LaFleur's scheme, but he said Iowa runs a similar outside-zone system. He hopes that will accelerate Johnson's transition.

In the meantime, the Packers also will rely heavily on young tailback MarShawn Lloyd. A 2024 third-round draft pick, Lloyd has played only 10 snaps in his first two NFL seasons because of injuries, but he exited training camp healthy. Part of the process of keeping him healthy was light work in the preseason. Lloyd had just 10 carries for 30 yards in a pair of preseason games before being shut down for the finale against Arizona. He added an 11-yard touchdown catch on the opening drive at the Denver Broncos.

"He's as ready as he's ever been since he's been here," Gutekunst said. "He looks good. He's handling all the physicality, the things that he needs to as a running back. I think it was good to get him out there and feel that. I think one of the things, particularly running backs or ball carriers, receivers, tight ends, when they haven't played a lot, just protecting the ball, taking the hits, all those kinds of things it takes. You need some of that to be ready. I think he's ready. I think he's obviously really eager.

"He's a running back in the National Football League. To think that he's not going to get dinged up and play through that going forward would be naïve. I think his mind is right, he's ready to go, and we're excited to see what he can do. I think each week he can be out there, you're going to see the better and better of MarShawn."

title: Köln set to return Crystal Palace fullback Sosa to Bundesliga

Former VfB Stuttgart defender Borna Sosa reached a verbal agreement for a loan move to Köln from Crystal Palace. The Bundesliga club are hoping to sort the final details in the coming hours. The Croat left the Bundesliga in 2023 with an €8 million move to Ajax Amsterdam.

At Köln, he'll compete with fellow summer signing Gideon Mensah for the spot yet to be filled since the retirement of club legend Jonas Hector. Sky Sports reported the loan deal will not have a purchase option.

title: Did the 49ers sign their Sky Moore of 2026 on the practice squad?
description: Brandon Codrington could be the 49ers annual buy low in August move that pays off all season.
fullText:
The most recent practice squad update for the San Francisco 49ers might end up being their most valuable. The team added Brandong Codrington, who spent the previous two seasons with the Buffalo Bills.

On the surface, Codrington has modest defensive numbers, but was an all-rookie returner. Then you connect the dots after reading that Jacob Cowing — the 49ers returner — was working on the side of practice on Monday as he recovers from a groin injury, and it makes sense why the 49ers would want to invest in Codrington.

This job belonged to Skyy Moore a year ago. Kyle Shanahan seemed enamored with Moore's ability to, for lack of a better word, hit the hole recklessly.

If Cowing isn't ready for Week 1, that leaves Deebo Samuel and Jordan Watkins as the returners. Deebo has proven to be a fantastic option, but he also may be involved in the offense more than anticipated after all of the injuries suffered at the position over the past month.

It would be special teams coordinator Brant Boyer's call. He's seen Watkins and Codrington return. Boyer witnessed Codrington have an explosive return during his tenure with the Jets. That year, Codrington had multiple returns that led him to being in the top 5 in both punt and kickoff return average:

Codrington finished top 5 in the league in punt and kickoff return average in '24. He had 2 kickoff returns of 50+ yards and 4 punt returns of 20+ yards in the last 2 seasons. 1 of those came against Brant Boyer's Jets.

If Jacob Cowing isn't ready, this could be the returner. https://t.co/DzxyehCUK2 pic.twitter.com/Qkf8zDVN9H

That looks different than what we've seen, albeit in a smaller sample size, when Watkins has the ball in his hands as a returner.

The team could elevate Codrington from the practice squad up to three times. If he's impressed enough by then, the Niners would be forced to sign Codrington to the active roster. If not, ideally, Cowing is healthy, and you have your original returner back.

You're always evaluating and trying to improve your team. That's what this move would be for the 49ers if they feel like Codrington offers more as a returner than Watkins — or Cowing, for that matter.

The team bought low on Moore last year, and it paid off. A few years ago, they did the same with Tashaun Gipson, and that ended up being one of the most important moves of the year. They're hoping for similar results this time around with Codrington.

title: Maple Leafs could unlock Auston Matthews with HC Jim Hiller’s new approach
description: Auston Matthews could see a larger offensive focus.
fullText:
The Toronto Maple Leafs could give Auston Matthews a bigger offensive role under new head coach Jim Hiller.

Matthews' usage next season is "forecasted to change" from previous NHL seasons, according to reporter Chris Johnston. That change could help Toronto get more from its captain.

"I forecast that Jim Hiller is going to probably change his usage a little bit," Johnston said. "And find opportunities where Auston's offensive gifts maybe are accentuated more than was the case under Craig Berube. I think that's entirely possible."

MORE: Maple Leafs linked to Penguins D-man Erik Karlsson in latest NHL buzz

That approach could matter after Matthews endured a difficult 2025-26 campaign. He scored 27 goals and 53 points in 60 games before an MCL injury ended his season. He has witnessed a gradual decline from his 69-goal season in 2023-24.

The Maple Leafs also missed the playoffs last year after finishing last in the Atlantic Division. Their coaching change now gives Hiller a chance to reshape how Toronto deploys its best player.

Matthews remains one of the NHL's elite goal scorers when healthy. The challenge involves creating more chances without weakening the team's defensive structure.

Toronto Maple Leafs center Auston Matthews (34) celebrates at Lenovo Center. Mandatory Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images

Johnston pointed toward several areas that could drive Matthews' rebound. "Perhaps a renewed look from the coaching staff in terms of how he's used and what offensive situations he's given," could create more offensive opportunities.

He also highlighted Toronto's power play. "Leafs power play improves," Johnston said, adding that these changes could return Matthews to the league's top offensive tier.

He said, "All these things… lead you back to a world where he's among the better offensive players in the game, as he has been multiple seasons in the past."

That assessment fits the Maple Leafs' larger need. Toronto cannot afford another season where their most important offensive player spends too much time away from dangerous scoring areas.

Hiller should likely favor targeted changes rather than abandoning Matthews' two-way responsibilities. Matthews can still handle difficult defensive assignments, but his offensive deployment should maximize his shooting ability.

MORE: Ex-Maple Leafs enforcer claims Morgan Rielly was 'panicking' last season

The departure of Mitch Marner changed Toronto's offensive structure last year. But after the arrival of No. 1 Pick Gavin McKenna, and if he gradually builds chemistry with Matthews, things can improve for the Maple Leafs' top scorer. He needs more touches to become the clear focal point during key offensive sequences.

Hiller therefore has a major tactical decision ahead. If he creates cleaner power-play looks and more offensive-zone opportunities, Matthews could regain his previous scoring form.

With the 2026-27 season approaching, Toronto needs its captain healthy, productive, and central to its attack.

title: Jeffery Simmons' 'feed my family' mentality is a recipe for success
description: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons explains his "feed my family" mentality.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans are gearing up for the start of the regular season on September 13, and as roster changes are happening, there is one player who remains the steadfast face of the team: Jeffery Simmons.

As the longest-tenured Titan on the roster, Simmons has become the unequivocal face of the franchise, and he is likely to remain so as long as he is with the team. One of the reasons Simmons is the face is because of his dominance on the defensive side of the ball, but it's also because he puts the success of the team before his own stats.

Recently, he spoke with Josh Chambers on The Pivot podcast and discussed his "feed my family" mentality.

Jeffrey Simmons explains his “feed my family” mentality and says he stopped setting sack goals because it caused him to hurt his own team's defense

“When I step on the field, I don’t care about anything else but how can I be the best for my team? My first couple years in the… pic.twitter.com/wHUvDOg9lM

"When I step on the field, I don't care about anything else but how can I be the best for my team?" Simmons said. "My first couple years in the league, it was, 'Let me set a goal. Let me set a goal for 10 sacks a year. Let me set a goal for this many tackles for loss.' But it took me away from the main goal. Once the game gets going and it's the fourth quarter, I don't have a sack, I don't have a tackle for loss, now I'm chasing plays. Now I'm hurting the defense by jumping out of the gap trying to make a play.

"So as I got older, especially last year, my thing was, how can I really focus on being in the moment? Make the play when it's there. Celebrate my teammate, because I know I'm going to get the slide. I know I'm going to get double-teamed, triple-teamed. But when my opportunity comes to make that play, I can't not be ready for it. Even when a double team comes, how can I create a one-on-one, even on a double team?

"How can I get to the center? How can I get to a different level to affect the game, affect the quarterback? That's just my mindset when I touch the field. I see red. You got a different color on. It's red. You in my way; you're trying to stop me from feeding my family. That's just the way I see the game."

Simmons' larger-than-life personality and overall size earned him the nickname Big Jeff. Opponents know what Big Jeff brings to the table; that's why he knows he's going to get double and triple-teamed on certain plays. But he also knows that when that happens, it means one or more of his teammates has an opportunity to make a play. That's how his "feed my family" mentality was born.

When players on a team are more focused on how they can improve the team and how they can help the team win than on their individual success, that's how a team starts winning. That's how a team starts seeing success.

The Titans have a new coaching staff in 2026, and they have new faces on the roster on both sides of the ball. But when you have leaders like Jeffery Simmons and Cam Ward out there making sure the team comes before their individual success, other players take notice. They start focusing on the team, too. And it might take some time because of all the new faces, but they'll start seeing wins, too.
